To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
two new assays based on virus pseudotype entry provide a sensitive, safe, and rapid method for detection of neutralization antibodies against Venezuelan equene encephalitis viruses.
we have developed a safe and rapid assay that detects antibodies to Venezuelan equine encepalitis virus and is a good substitute for the conventional assay that uses live virus.
we have developed two assays that are safe, sensitive and in general recapitalize neutralizing antibody titres obtained by conventional plaque-reduction assays.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of new technologies to the detection and characterization of antibodies to Venezuelan equine encepalitis virus.
the development and application of novel diagnostic tools to detect antibodies against Venezuelan equines encephalitis (VEE) viruses.
the development of new assays for the detection of neutralizing antibody against Venezuelan equine encaphalitis virus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pseudotype assay provides an alternative to the traditional plaque reduction neutralization assay, which is the gold standard for the detection of VEEV neutralizing antibodies.
the use of pseudotyped viruses for the detection of VEEV-specific neutralizing antibodies is a rapid and reliable alternative to the traditional plaque reduction neutralization test.
pseudotype assays are rapid and safe, but not as sensitive as conventional plaque reduction assays for detection of neutralization of Venezuelan equine equine encephalis virus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pseudotypes are an excellent alternative to conventional neutralization assays for the study of Venezuelan equine virus and other viruses.
pseudotyped viruses can be used as a rapid and safe alternative to conventional assays for the detection of neutralizing antibody against Venezuelan equine equine encephalphalitis virus.

the pseudotype assays can detect neutralizing antibodies in serum samples against all VEEV subtypes, including those for which no neutralization assays are currently available, and that they can be used to distinguish VEEV from other alphaviruses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pseudotype assays can be performed in any laboratory with access to a biosafety level 2 containment hood and are a safe alternative to conventional neutralization assays.

the pseudotypes we describe can be used for rapid detection of antibodies against any enveloped virus, including those that are difficult to work with due to high biosafety levels, high pathogenicity, and/or high select agent security levels.
pseudotyped viruses can be used to detect neutralizing antibodies against any virus.
